scripts.name: Ananya Iyer
scripts.profile: Full credit — complete, correctly reasoned answers to all three questions.
scripts.tests: Correct answer: every rubric point should be CORRECT and the total should be the paper maximum.

scripts.name: Rohit Menon
scripts.profile: Partial credit — the core idea of each question is there, but the instrument placement, the counter-argument and the cost-shift analysis are all missing.
scripts.tests: Partial answer: marks should be awarded proportionally, with the missing rubric points named rather than silently rolled into the total.

scripts.name: Kabir Shah
scripts.profile: Confidently wrong — voltmeter in series, resistance stated to increase current, equilibrium read off the wrong row, and an English answer that asserts without support.
scripts.tests: Incorrect answer: near-zero marks, and every wrong statement should come back with a correction rather than only a lost mark.

scripts.name: Sana Qureshi
scripts.profile: Effectively blank — the script was handed in with only the headings copied out.
scripts.tests: Blank answer: every rubric point should be MISSING with zero marks, and the run must not invent evidence boxes for text that is not on the page.

scripts.name: Devansh Rao
scripts.profile: Correct content carried through a poor scan — the same substance as TR-01, degraded with the character confusions a real OCR pass produces (rn/m, l/1, 0/O, split words).
scripts.tests: OCR noise: evidence should still be located by fuzzy match, and marks should not collapse because of spelling damage.

scripts.name: Meera Krishnan
scripts.profile: Strong overall, one clean gap — Q3 never explains what happens away from equilibrium, which should cost exactly one rubric point and no more.
scripts.tests: A single missing rubric point must be isolated to that point, not spread across the question.

scripts.name: Aarav Bansal
scripts.profile: Argues the opposite conclusion to the model answer for Q2, but argues it properly — position, development, counter-view, example, conclusion.
scripts.tests: The grader must reward quality of reasoning, not similarity to the model answer. A well-argued disagreement should still score 5/5 on Q2.

scripts.name: Zoya Farooqui
scripts.profile: Long but empty — restates the question at length, repeats itself, and rarely commits to a testable claim.
scripts.tests: Length must not be mistaken for correctness: marks should track the rubric points actually satisfied.

scripts.name: Nikhil Prasad
scripts.profile: Ran out of time — Q2 answered properly, Q1 abandoned after two lines, Q3 not started.
scripts.tests: A blank question inside an otherwise answered script must be MISSING on its own points without dragging down the answered ones.

scripts.name: Tanvi Deshmukh
scripts.profile: Draws well, writes almost nothing — correct diagrams for Q1 and Q3 with only label-level text, so most explanation points are unsupported.
scripts.tests: Marks that depend on an explanation should not be awarded from a correct diagram alone; the feedback should say what the writing was missing.

scripts.name: Imran Sheikh
scripts.profile: Sound method, wrong number — reads the equilibrium off the wrong row of the schedule and then reasons correctly from that wrong value.
scripts.tests: The grader has to catch a factual error inside otherwise correct reasoning, and quote the sentence that contains it.

scripts.name: Preeti Nair
scripts.profile: Worst-case scan — correct answers under heavy character substitution, hyphenated line breaks and a stray scanner artefact line.
scripts.tests: Stress case for evidence location: quotes must still be matched, and where a quote genuinely cannot be located no box should be drawn.
